bull_bear.body: Three-pronged approach: 1) Increase shareholder returns (Dividend INR 8/share, +33% YoY); 2) Fund committed annuity capex; 3) Opportunistic, margin-accretive land deals. Dividend largely fueled by DCCDL cash flows.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution delays in experience center/launches; Macro headwinds (Iran-US war mentioned as potential tenant decision deferrer, though no direct impact yet); SEZ vacancy (17-20% in Hyderabad, overall portfolio vacancy cost down to 3.5%); Regulatory delays (Goa PIL).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Disciplined, confident, and shareholder-return focused. Explicitly rejects chasing presale volume metrics in favor of margins and cash flows. Emphasizes delivery capability constraints in the industry as a reason for calibrated launches.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management revealed that super-luxury pricing in Gurugram (Dahlias/Camellias) has caught up to or exceeded South Mumbai levels (INR 150k-160k/sq ft carpet area). Two-thirds of the dividend payout is derived from DCCDL's cash flows, highlighting the subsidiary's role as a cash cow. The 'INR 60,000 cr pipeline' is a subset of a larger INR 1,14,000 cr 5-year plan, phased to match absorption and execution capacity.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Stated philosophy: "Surplus cash being allocated for dividend payout and growth capex" and "Increasing shareholder returns continues to be an integral part of the allocation".
- DLF Limited is net cash positive — net cash position of INR 15,200 cr (of which Rs 11,305 cr sits in RERA 70% accounts and Rs 3,895 cr other cash balances) — against DCCDL net debt of INR 18,136 cr at Net Debt/EBITDA 3.1 and Net Debt/GAV 0.18.
- Group credit ratings of ICRA AAA/Stable and CRISIL AAA/Stable; DCCDL's Net Debt/EBITDA has fallen 4.5 (FY23) to 3.1 (Q1FY27) and Net Debt/GAV from 26% to 18% over the same periods.
- Surplus cash potential from launched products as on 30.06.2026 is ~Rs 43,650 crore — ~Rs 27,000 crore from sales already done plus ~Rs 16,650 crore from launched-but-unsold inventory.
- Cash moves up from the rental entity via dividend: DCCDL paid a Rs 1,771 crore dividend in Q4FY26, of which DLF recorded Rs 1,180 crore inflow; no dividend flowed either way in Q1FY27.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Trusted, credible developer with a proven execution track record, which the sector is consolidating around (scale, brand, delivery)
- Industry-leading annuity occupancy of ~95% across a ~4.65 msm (~50 msf) operational rental portfolio, underscoring quality and resilience of the platform
- Achieved zero gross debt in the development business, reinforcing balance sheet strength and a net cash position of ₹14,155 crore
- Credit ratings upgraded during the year to CRISIL AA+/Stable and ICRA AA+/Stable, reflecting a strengthening credit profile
- Large residual development potential of ~12.74 msm (~137 msf, including TOD/TDR) beyond the identified launch pipeline, providing long-term growth visibility
- Diversified launch pipeline and financial discipline cited as key mitigants against operating and market risks
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Macro-economic sensitivity — Inflationary pressures from global energy market disruptions, interest rate volatility and geopolitical developments (particularly the ongoing conflict in West Asia) may influence customer sentiment, construction costs and capital allocation.
- Regulatory exposure — The business remains exposed to changes in development guidelines, environmental clearance processes, taxation frameworks and zoning regulations that can affect project viability and timelines.
- Execution and operational risk — Management monitors risks associated with execution delays, supply chain disruptions and cyber security threats that may impact business continuity and stakeholder trust.
- Legal/contractual dispute (IL&FS) — A Section 9 IBC petition was filed by IL&FS Engineering and Construction Company Limited relating to a road project contract at Sector 56, Gurugram; DLF separately submitted counter-claims. The parties agreed to settle all disputes and withdraw inter-se proceedings pursuant to a Settlement Agreement dated 23 March 2026, pending payment of the settlement amount.
- Office-segment demand monitoring: geopolitics and AI impact — While the office outlook is constructive, geopolitical developments and the evolving impact of artificial intelligence on occupier demand were flagged by management as factors that warrant monitoring for institutional-grade office assets.
- General forward-looking-statement risk factors — The MD&A's cautionary statement flags risks and uncertainties including fluctuations in earnings, the Company's ability to manage growth, competition, economic growth in India, ability to attract and retain highly skilled professionals, time and cost overruns on contracts, and Government policies/actions on investments, fiscal deficits and regulations.
- Enterprise risk governance dependency — DLF relies on a structured Enterprise Risk Management framework and business-unit-level risk registers reviewed by senior management and the Risk Management Committee; the Company cites its diversified launch pipeline, financial discipline and governance culture as key mitigants against emerging risks.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Residential: Super-luxury 'Dahlias' averaging INR 135 cr/unit, prices appreciating from INR 60-75 cr to INR 90-110 cr in 1.5 years. Rental: 50 mn sq ft portfolio, 95% occupancy. Office: Non-SEZ 98-99% occupied, SEZ 88-89%. Retail: Midtown Plaza (95% leased), Summit Plaza (95-97% leased, opening July), Promenade Goa (50% leased, opening Aug).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "We operate as a diversified enterprise having significant presence in both Development and Annuity businesses enabling the organization to operate with a remarkably differentiated model" — development delivering high margins and strong cash flows, rental providing consistently growing income, with hospitality and services/asset management complementing both.
- Claims a "Demonstrated track record of 8 decades of customer centricity" and best-practice governance/safety compliance "resulting in a Strong Brand positioning", supported by a "high-quality land bank" and "integrated ecosystems offering superior products".
- Annuity platform described as "One of the largest organically grown Annuity Platform", operating at 95% occupancy by area and 97% by value — "highest in the industry" per the deck.
- Group structure: DLF Limited holds DLF Home Developers Limited [100%], other subsidiaries [100%], DCCDL [66.67%] and Atrium Place [67%], with JVs at Midtown Delhi (DMPL, 50%) and Mumbai (51%).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [TOD/TDR policy] The deck flags "significant upside from TOD/TDR policy" and states that both the development land bank (188 msf) and annuity balance potential (60 msf) are revised estimates that now include TOD/TDR potential.
- [Accounting basis] DLF Limited figures are consolidated but DCCDL and other JVs are not consolidated line-by-line — only DLF's share of profit/loss is accounted; group-overview figures "include the entire business and do not account for any minority interests".
- [Proforma caveat] Segmental bifurcation, surplus-cash and gross-margin figures are management best estimates, "should not be construed as audited financial information" and are subject to market conditions.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: DLF develops and sells residential real estate (high-rise condominiums, low-rise independent floors, plotted development and shop-cum-offices) and operates a diversified annuity business comprising office leasing, retail mall leasing, asset management (CAM/services) and a hospitality vertical (hotels, clubs, F&B). Its customers are individual home-buyers and businesses/occupiers (including GCCs, technology, flex-space and BFSI tenants) across major Indian cities, with 100% of turnover from real estate activities carried out with own or leased property.

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin ~46% (Q4), ~39% (FY26). Brokerage costs linked to collections caused Q4 spike; overheads normalizing. Focus on INR 9,000-10,000 cr annual margin creation rather than maximizing presale volume.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Mid-teens NOI growth for rental business; Margin: Targeting INR 9,000-10,000 cr annual margin creation; Order Inflow: ~INR 20,000 cr annual sales guidance (calibrated, not volume-chasing); Capex/Commissioning: Atrium Place OC Q2FY27, 3 Malls operational H2FY27, Downtown Taramani completion Q2FY27, Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 completion FY28-29.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Sales bookings FY26: INR 20,143 cr. Key drivers: Sellout of Privana North (Gurugram), West Park (Mumbai), and 32 units of Dahlias (Q4). Launch pipeline for FY27: ~INR 20,000 cr including Senior Living, Hamilton 2, West Park Phase 2, and continued Dahlias sales.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Land bank of 137 mn sq ft (40 mn sq ft in North/Metros) monetizable over 5-10 years. Upcoming launches: Arbour Senior Living, Hamilton 2 (Gurugram), Goa project (approvals done, PIL pending), West Park Phase 2 (Mumbai). Potential for upward revision in sales guidance if demand sustains.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Strategy anchored on customer centricity, premium product positioning, execution excellence, disciplined capital allocation, balance sheet strength and cash flow-led growth
- Calibrated approach to bringing high quality new products across key focus markets, prioritising a launch pipeline that delivers healthy gross margins and cash generation
- Prudent capital allocation framework that balances growth investments with shareholder returns
- Continues to deploy capital judiciously to expand the rental (annuity) platform in line with stated guidance
- Annuity business strategy spans four verticals: development and leasing of offices, development and leasing of retail malls, asset management (CAM/Services), and hospitality (Hotels, Clubs, Food & Beverages)
- The Notice of AGM records a Board-recommended dividend of ₹8 per equity share (400% of the ₹2 face value) for FY 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM and deduction of tax at source, consistent with the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy under SEBI Listing Regulations. Beyond the dividend recommendation, this bundle does not disclose further capital-allocation philosophy (e.g., debt-reduction or reinvestment policy detail sits in the Board's Report / MD&A rather than the governance-entities routed sections).
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: DLF's development business added to its launch pipeline with 'The Westpark' in Mumbai (its maiden launch in that geography) and continued strong response to 'DLF Privana North' (Sector 76-77, Gurugram, a successful sell-out) and 'The Dahlias' (DLF5, Gurugram, super-luxury). On the annuity side, the operational rental portfolio was expanded during the fiscal with four new asset additions: DLF Downtown, Chennai (Block 3, ~1.1 msf, with strong pre-leasing), Atrium Place, Gurugram (Phase 1, ~2.1 msf), Summit Plaza, Gurugram (~0.5 msf) and Midtown Plaza, New Delhi (~0.2 msf). The Company also completed the divestment of its IT/ITeS SEZ undertaking along with a vacant land parcel in Kolkata during the fiscal for a total consideration of ₹710.23 crore. Separately, capex directed at environmental/social improvement (energy-efficient chillers and chiller pumps across rental properties, Organic Waste Converter machines at rental and hospitality properties) accounted for 1.04% of total capex in FY 2025-26, versus 1.16% in FY 2024-25.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Residential outlook remains constructive, supported by favourable demographics, urbanisation, infrastructure expansion and resilient premium demand; demand in premium and luxury segments expected to remain healthy, especially for integrated, well-located developments from credible brands
- Sector consolidation continues in favour of scale, brand and delivery track record, favouring trusted developers with proven execution capability
- Office outlook remains constructive, supported by India's cost competitiveness, deep talent base and rising GCC penetration, though geopolitical developments and the evolving impact of artificial intelligence warrant monitoring
- Retail outlook remains positive, supported by rising consumption, premiumisation and sustained demand for investment-grade retail assets, translating into resilient occupancy and steady rental growth
- Annuity business well positioned for steady growth, supported by India's rising role in global business services, sustained GCC demand and continuing premiumisation in organised retail — structural drivers supporting both rental escalation and portfolio expansion
- Identified new-product launch pipeline with total sales potential of ₹1.14 lakh crore, of which ~₹54,285 crore of new launches have already been done till FY 2025-26, with the balance to be brought to market
- Residual development potential (development business) of ~12.74 msm (~137 msf), including TOD and TDR potential, beyond the identified launch pipeline
- Annuity business has additional residual development potential of ~5.58 msm (~60 msf), including TOD/TDR potential, beyond the current pipeline

deepdive.thesis: DLF delivered a record collection of INR 13,500 cr and zero gross debt in development, while shifting focus from volume-led presales to margin/cash-flow optimization with the super-luxury 'Dahlias' project driving price discovery. The annuity business is entering a high-growth phase with 34-35% NOI growth, supported by full leasing of new assets like Atrium Place, ensuring a dual-engine growth model of high-margin sales and compounding rental income.

Beyond the dividend recommendation, this bundle does not disclose further capital-allocation philosophy (e.g., debt-reduction or reinvestment policy detail sits in the Board's Report / MD&A rather than the governance-entities routed sections).
currentContext.expansion: DLF's development business added to its launch pipeline with 'The Westpark' in Mumbai (its maiden launch in that geography) and continued strong response to 'DLF Privana North' (Sector 76-77, Gurugram, a successful sell-out) and 'The Dahlias' (DLF5, Gurugram, super-luxury). The Company also completed the divestment of its IT/ITeS SEZ undertaking along with a vacant land parcel in Kolkata during the fiscal for a total consideration of ₹710.23 crore. Separately, capex directed at environmental/social improvement (energy-efficient chillers and chiller pumps across rental properties, Organic Waste Converter machines at rental and hospitality properties) accounted for 1.04% of total capex in FY 2025-26, versus 1.16% in FY 2024-25.

risks.note: Inflationary pressures from global energy market disruptions, interest rate volatility and geopolitical developments (particularly the ongoing conflict in West Asia) may influence customer sentiment, construction costs and capital allocation.
The business remains exposed to changes in development guidelines, environmental clearance processes, taxation frameworks and zoning regulations that can affect project viability and timelines.
Management monitors risks associated with execution delays, supply chain disruptions and cyber security threats that may impact business continuity and stakeholder trust.

A Section 9 IBC petition was filed by IL&FS Engineering and Construction Company Limited relating to a road project contract at Sector 56, Gurugram; DLF separately submitted counter-claims. The parties agreed to settle all disputes and withdraw inter-se proceedings pursuant to a Settlement Agreement dated 23 March 2026, pending payment of the settlement amount.

risks.risk: Office-segment demand monitoring: geopolitics and AI impact
risks.note: While the office outlook is constructive, geopolitical developments and the evolving impact of artificial intelligence on occupier demand were flagged by management as factors that warrant monitoring for institutional-grade office assets.

The MD&A's cautionary statement flags risks and uncertainties including fluctuations in earnings, the Company's ability to manage growth, competition, economic growth in India, ability to attract and retain highly skilled professionals, time and cost overruns on contracts, and Government policies/actions on investments, fiscal deficits and regulations.

DLF relies on a structured Enterprise Risk Management framework and business-unit-level risk registers reviewed by senior management and the Risk Management Committee; the Company cites its diversified launch pipeline, financial discipline and governance culture as key mitigants against emerging risks.

one-line thesis: DLF delivered a record collection of INR 13,500 cr and zero gross debt in development, while shifting focus from volume-led presales to margin/cash-flow optimization with the super-luxury 'Dahlias' project driving price discovery. The annuity business is entering a high-growth phase with 34-35% NOI growth, supported by full leasing of new assets like Atrium Place, ensuring a dual-engine growth model of high-margin sales and compounding rental income.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 2,452 cr (Q4), ~INR 10,000 cr (FY26); EBITDA: >INR 3,000 cr (FY26), Gross Margin ~39% (FY26); PAT: INR 4,408 cr (reported, ex-exception), INR 4,256 cr (net, +16% YoY); Order Book: Sales bookings INR 20,143 cr (FY26), Q4 sales INR 3,967 cr; Net Debt: Zero gross debt in development business, Net Cash INR 14,155 cr (INR 11,200 cr in RERA escrow). One-offs: Marketing/brokerage costs spiked in Q4 due to milestone payouts on prior robust collections; Tax refunds from accumulated losses recognized.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Mid-teens NOI growth for rental business; Margin: Targeting INR 9,000-10,000 cr annual margin creation; Order Inflow: ~INR 20,000 cr annual sales guidance (calibrated, not volume-chasing); Capex/Commissioning: Atrium Place OC Q2FY27, 3 Malls operational H2FY27, Downtown Taramani completion Q2FY27, Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 completion FY28-29.
order book & pipeline: Sales bookings FY26: INR 20,143 cr. Key drivers: Sellout of Privana North (Gurugram), West Park (Mumbai), and 32 units of Dahlias (Q4). Launch pipeline for FY27: ~INR 20,000 cr including Senior Living, Hamilton 2, West Park Phase 2, and continued Dahlias sales.
segment / subsidiary detail: Residential: Super-luxury 'Dahlias' averaging INR 135 cr/unit, prices appreciating from INR 60-75 cr to INR 90-110 cr in 1.5 years. Rental: 50 mn sq ft portfolio, 95% occupancy. Office: Non-SEZ 98-99% occupied, SEZ 88-89%. Retail: Midtown Plaza (95% leased), Summit Plaza (95-97% leased, opening July), Promenade Goa (50% leased, opening Aug).
growth verticals / optionality: Land bank of 137 mn sq ft (40 mn sq ft in North/Metros) monetizable over 5-10 years. Upcoming launches: Arbour Senior Living, Hamilton 2 (Gurugram), Goa project (approvals done, PIL pending), West Park Phase 2 (Mumbai). Potential for upward revision in sales guidance if demand sustains.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin ~46% (Q4), ~39% (FY26). Brokerage costs linked to collections caused Q4 spike; overheads normalizing. Focus on INR 9,000-10,000 cr annual margin creation rather than maximizing presale volume.
capex / expansion: Committed capex for annuity portfolio expansion (Atrium Place, 3 Malls, Downtown Taramani, Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2). No specific INR figure provided, but funded by strong operating cash flows and existing cash reserves.
capital allocation: Three-pronged approach: 1) Increase shareholder returns (Dividend INR 8/share, +33% YoY); 2) Fund committed annuity capex; 3) Opportunistic, margin-accretive land deals. Dividend largely fueled by DCCDL cash flows.
risks & watch-items: Execution delays in experience center/launches; Macro headwinds (Iran-US war mentioned as potential tenant decision deferrer, though no direct impact yet); SEZ vacancy (17-20% in Hyderabad, overall portfolio vacancy cost down to 3.5%); Regulatory delays (Goa PIL).
management quality / tone: Disciplined, confident, and shareholder-return focused. Explicitly rejects chasing presale volume metrics in favor of margins and cash flows. Emphasizes delivery capability constraints in the industry as a reason for calibrated launches.
non-obvious takeaways: Management revealed that super-luxury pricing in Gurugram (Dahlias/Camellias) has caught up to or exceeded South Mumbai levels (INR 150k-160k/sq ft carpet area). Two-thirds of the dividend payout is derived from DCCDL's cash flows, highlighting the subsidiary's role as a cash cow. The 'INR 60,000 cr pipeline' is a subset of a larger INR 1,14,000 cr 5-year plan, phased to match absorption and execution capacity.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: DLF is India's leading real estate developer, running a development business (residential condominiums, floors, plots) alongside a large annuity platform (office and retail leasing, asset management and hospitality) anchored by DLF Cyber City Developers Limited (DCCDL).

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: DLF develops and sells residential real estate (high-rise condominiums, low-rise independent floors, plotted development and shop-cum-offices) and operates a diversified annuity business comprising office leasing, retail mall leasing, asset management (CAM/services) and a hospitality vertical (hotels, clubs, F&B). Its customers are individual home-buyers and businesses/occupiers (including GCCs, technology, flex-space and BFSI tenants) across major Indian cities, with 100% of turnover from real estate activities carried out with own or leased property.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Residential outlook remains constructive, supported by favourable demographics, urbanisation, infrastructure expansion and resilient premium demand; demand in premium and luxury segments expected to remain healthy, especially for integrated, well-located developments from credible brands
- Sector consolidation continues in favour of scale, brand and delivery track record, favouring trusted developers with proven execution capability
- Office outlook remains constructive, supported by India's cost competitiveness, deep talent base and rising GCC penetration, though geopolitical developments and the evolving impact of artificial intelligence warrant monitoring
- Retail outlook remains positive, supported by rising consumption, premiumisation and sustained demand for investment-grade retail assets, translating into resilient occupancy and steady rental growth
- Annuity business well positioned for steady growth, supported by India's rising role in global business services, sustained GCC demand and continuing premiumisation in organised retail — structural drivers supporting both rental escalation and portfolio expansion
- Identified new-product launch pipeline with total sales potential of ₹1.14 lakh crore, of which ~₹54,285 crore of new launches have already been done till FY 2025-26, with the balance to be brought to market
- Residual development potential (development business) of ~12.74 msm (~137 msf), including TOD and TDR potential, beyond the identified launch pipeline
- Annuity business has additional residual development potential of ~5.58 msm (~60 msf), including TOD/TDR potential, beyond the current pipeline

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin ~46% (Q4), ~39% (FY26). Brokerage costs linked to collections caused Q4 spike; overheads normalizing. Focus on INR 9,000-10,000 cr annual margin creation rather than maximizing presale volume.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Three-pronged approach: 1) Increase shareholder returns (Dividend INR 8/share, +33% YoY); 2) Fund committed annuity capex; 3) Opportunistic, margin-accretive land deals. Dividend largely fueled by DCCDL cash flows.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: DLF's development business added to its launch pipeline with 'The Westpark' in Mumbai (its maiden launch in that geography) and continued strong response to 'DLF Privana North' (Sector 76-77, Gurugram, a successful sell-out) and 'The Dahlias' (DLF5, Gurugram, super-luxury). On the annuity side, the operational rental portfolio was expanded during the fiscal with four new asset additions: DLF Downtown, Chennai (Block 3, ~1.1 msf, with strong pre-leasing), Atrium Place, Gurugram (Phase 1, ~2.1 msf), Summit Plaza, Gurugram (~0.5 msf) and Midtown Plaza, New Delhi (~0.2 msf). The Company also completed the divestment of its IT/ITeS SEZ undertaking along with a vacant land parcel in Kolkata during the fiscal for a total consideration of ₹710.23 crore. Separately, capex directed at environmental/social improvement (energy-efficient chillers and chiller pumps across rental properties, Organic Waste Converter machines at rental and hospitality properties) accounted for 1.04% of total capex in FY 2025-26, versus 1.16% in FY 2024-25.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Disciplined, confident, and shareholder-return focused. Explicitly rejects chasing presale volume metrics in favor of margins and cash flows. Emphasizes delivery capability constraints in the industry as a reason for calibrated launches.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Trusted, credible developer with a proven execution track record, which the sector is consolidating around (scale, brand, delivery)
- Industry-leading annuity occupancy of ~95% across a ~4.65 msm (~50 msf) operational rental portfolio, underscoring quality and resilience of the platform
- Achieved zero gross debt in the development business, reinforcing balance sheet strength and a net cash position of ₹14,155 crore
- Credit ratings upgraded during the year to CRISIL AA+/Stable and ICRA AA+/Stable, reflecting a strengthening credit profile
- Large residual development potential of ~12.74 msm (~137 msf, including TOD/TDR) beyond the identified launch pipeline, providing long-term growth visibility
- Diversified launch pipeline and financial discipline cited as key mitigants against operating and market risks

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Execution delays in experience center/launches; Macro headwinds (Iran-US war mentioned as potential tenant decision deferrer, though no direct impact yet); SEZ vacancy (17-20% in Hyderabad, overall portfolio vacancy cost down to 3.5%); Regulatory delays (Goa PIL).

non_obvious.body: Management revealed that super-luxury pricing in Gurugram (Dahlias/Camellias) has caught up to or exceeded South Mumbai levels (INR 150k-160k/sq ft carpet area). Two-thirds of the dividend payout is derived from DCCDL's cash flows, highlighting the subsidiary's role as a cash cow. The 'INR 60,000 cr pipeline' is a subset of a larger INR 1,14,000 cr 5-year plan, phased to match absorption and execution capacity.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [TOD/TDR policy] The deck flags "significant upside from TOD/TDR policy" and states that both the development land bank (188 msf) and annuity balance potential (60 msf) are revised estimates that now include TOD/TDR potential.
- [Accounting basis] DLF Limited figures are consolidated but DCCDL and other JVs are not consolidated line-by-line — only DLF's share of profit/loss is accounted; group-overview figures "include the entire business and do not account for any minority interests".
- [Proforma caveat] Segmental bifurcation, surplus-cash and gross-margin figures are management best estimates, "should not be construed as audited financial information" and are subject to market conditions.

one-line thesis: DLF delivered a record collection of INR 13,500 cr and zero gross debt in development, while shifting focus from volume-led presales to margin/cash-flow optimization with the super-luxury 'Dahlias' project driving price discovery. The annuity business is entering a high-growth phase with 34-35% NOI growth, supported by full leasing of new assets like Atrium Place, ensuring a dual-engine growth model of high-margin sales and compounding rental income.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 2,452 cr (Q4), ~INR 10,000 cr (FY26); EBITDA: >INR 3,000 cr (FY26), Gross Margin ~39% (FY26); PAT: INR 4,408 cr (reported, ex-exception), INR 4,256 cr (net, +16% YoY); Order Book: Sales bookings INR 20,143 cr (FY26), Q4 sales INR 3,967 cr; Net Debt: Zero gross debt in development business, Net Cash INR 14,155 cr (INR 11,200 cr in RERA escrow). One-offs: Marketing/brokerage costs spiked in Q4 due to milestone payouts on prior robust collections; Tax refunds from accumulated losses recognized.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Mid-teens NOI growth for rental business; Margin: Targeting INR 9,000-10,000 cr annual margin creation; Order Inflow: ~INR 20,000 cr annual sales guidance (calibrated, not volume-chasing); Capex/Commissioning: Atrium Place OC Q2FY27, 3 Malls operational H2FY27, Downtown Taramani completion Q2FY27, Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2 completion FY28-29.
order book & pipeline: Sales bookings FY26: INR 20,143 cr. Key drivers: Sellout of Privana North (Gurugram), West Park (Mumbai), and 32 units of Dahlias (Q4). Launch pipeline for FY27: ~INR 20,000 cr including Senior Living, Hamilton 2, West Park Phase 2, and continued Dahlias sales.
segment / subsidiary detail: Residential: Super-luxury 'Dahlias' averaging INR 135 cr/unit, prices appreciating from INR 60-75 cr to INR 90-110 cr in 1.5 years. Rental: 50 mn sq ft portfolio, 95% occupancy. Office: Non-SEZ 98-99% occupied, SEZ 88-89%. Retail: Midtown Plaza (95% leased), Summit Plaza (95-97% leased, opening July), Promenade Goa (50% leased, opening Aug).
growth verticals / optionality: Land bank of 137 mn sq ft (40 mn sq ft in North/Metros) monetizable over 5-10 years. Upcoming launches: Arbour Senior Living, Hamilton 2 (Gurugram), Goa project (approvals done, PIL pending), West Park Phase 2 (Mumbai). Potential for upward revision in sales guidance if demand sustains.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin ~46% (Q4), ~39% (FY26). Brokerage costs linked to collections caused Q4 spike; overheads normalizing. Focus on INR 9,000-10,000 cr annual margin creation rather than maximizing presale volume.
capex / expansion: Committed capex for annuity portfolio expansion (Atrium Place, 3 Malls, Downtown Taramani, Downtown Gurgaon Phase 2). No specific INR figure provided, but funded by strong operating cash flows and existing cash reserves.
capital allocation: Three-pronged approach: 1) Increase shareholder returns (Dividend INR 8/share, +33% YoY); 2) Fund committed annuity capex; 3) Opportunistic, margin-accretive land deals. Dividend largely fueled by DCCDL cash flows.
risks & watch-items: Execution delays in experience center/launches; Macro headwinds (Iran-US war mentioned as potential tenant decision deferrer, though no direct impact yet); SEZ vacancy (17-20% in Hyderabad, overall portfolio vacancy cost down to 3.5%); Regulatory delays (Goa PIL).
management quality / tone: Disciplined, confident, and shareholder-return focused. Explicitly rejects chasing presale volume metrics in favor of margins and cash flows. Emphasizes delivery capability constraints in the industry as a reason for calibrated launches.
non-obvious takeaways: Management revealed that super-luxury pricing in Gurugram (Dahlias/Camellias) has caught up to or exceeded South Mumbai levels (INR 150k-160k/sq ft carpet area). Two-thirds of the dividend payout is derived from DCCDL's cash flows, highlighting the subsidiary's role as a cash cow. The 'INR 60,000 cr pipeline' is a subset of a larger INR 1,14,000 cr 5-year plan, phased to match absorption and execution capacity.

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.
